pro_course_detail.title: Interview Coaching
pro_course_detail.description:
Prior to becoming a university professor, I worked in the business world. I was previously a recruiter for finance and accounting professionals and have also worked in marketing.  Through iTalki, I have worked with many global business professionals and academics to prepare for upcoming job interviews.

In our meetings, we will practice delivering effective and concise responses to various types of interview questions that go beyond technical questions related to your work (depending on your needs).  Although we can practice questions directly related to your line of work, we will most likely focus on mastering responses to questions including the following structures:
1) Tell me about yourself.
2) Tell me about a time when you. . . (describing past accomplishments and work experiences)
3) Two-part questions, e.g., Describe your leadership style, and tell me about a time where you successfully handled a conflict among your team members. 
4) Hypothetical questions, e.g., What would you do if you had an upcoming deadline that you most likely were not going to meet? 

Additionally, you can expect to receive feedback on the following: grammar, pronunciation, word choice, fluency, eye contact, body language, facial expressions, level of confidence, etc.

During our sessions, we will have a mock interview where I will assume the role of the hiring manager, and you will be the job candidate.  During the practice interview, I will take comprehensive notes on your performance. You will be provided the notes at the end of our session, and I can also give a video link to a recording of the practice interview (optional).

My Grammar Practice for adults worksheets are filled with useful, everyday language that will boost your grammar skills and help you develop your fluency. These lessons are a lifeline for any student looking for extra ways to reinforce a specific grammar point.

I also have Grammar Assessment Tests to determine your current English level. 

Grammar Test 1-Beg: a low or mid-range score indicates that students should use our beginner-level materials. A high score indicates that they can use low-intermediate or intermediate materials. 

Grammar Test 2-Low Int: a low or mid-range score indicates that students should use our beginner or low-intermediate materials. A high score indicates that they can use intermediate materials. 

Grammar Test 3 – Int: it is recommended that students get a high grade on Grammar Tests 1 and 2 before trying Test 3. For placement, a low or mid-range score on Grammar Test 3 indicates that students should use our intermediate-level materials. A high score indicates that they may be ready for high-intermediate or advanced materials. 

Grammar Test 4 - High Int – Adv: it is also recommended that students get a high grade on Grammar Tests 1, 2, and 3 before trying Test 4. For placement, a low or mid-range score on Grammar Test 4 indicates that students should use our intermediate – high-intermediate materials. A high score indicates that they can use advanced materials as well as authentic reading and listening materials.

pro_course_detail.title: Speak more like a native English speaker (Adults B1-C2) - Pronunciation, Common Expressions, Rhythm and more
pro_course_detail.description:
There are certain things that make it obvious that you're not a native English speaker. Pronunciation is only one small part of that.

In these sessions, I'll help you fully understand and improve all the areas that will help you speak more naturally like a native speaker.

We will cover:
- pronunciation (of course)
- common phrases, expressions & idioms (including what they mean, correct ways to say them, and appropriate times to use them + when not to use them)
- slang + which slang should not be used in a professional setting (you have to be careful with this)
- proper greetings + how to respond to different greetings
- appropriate greetings to use with your superiors vs. peers or subordinates (You want to be sure to get this right!)
- formal vs. informal language + appropriate times to use each one
- the correct rhythm of the English language + how it's different from your native language
- correct use of emphasis on words in a sentence to convey different meanings
- different ways to introduce yourself (or someone else) depending on if you're in person, on the phone, or via email
- correct use of prepositions, especially in/on/at (These can be confusing for non-native English speakers.)
- correct use of verb tenses (This is one of the biggest ways you can sound more natural right away.)
- how to properly pronounce letters when spelling words (and differences between British & American English)
- other differences between British & American English that you should know, especially depending on who you work with more often
- how to properly say numbers + how it's different depending on the type of number
- how to express units of measurement (like when to use things like carton, container, pack, package, etc.)
- and many more words, phrases, and ways to say things that will help you sound more natural when speaking

Having taught English for 14 years, I can quickly spot the areas you can improve to sound more natural. With my coaching, you will improve quickly.

pro_course_detail.title: CV and Presentation Proofreading/Coaching
pro_course_detail.description:
Your academic or professional experience can shine through and create a great impression of your talent and abilities, even if your English writing and speaking isn’t perfect. But if your errors are too serious, you risk giving the impression that communication with you could be problematic.

My knowledge of formal English writing, and experience with editing is more than sufficient to take your written work well beyond the ‘adequate’ level (Candidly, it’s no exaggeration to say that any capable editor can easily make it flawless, and sparkle like a jewel!) However, more modest improvements are often a wiser choice, to match the level of your conversational (and presentational) English skills. As we review and revise your written information together, your ability to express this information verbally (speaking and conversing) will naturally grow. You will find I am well prepared to guide this process – recognizing where my patience as a teacher is necessary, because the expression of such information may become quite complex.

pro_course_detail.title: American English Pronunciation Lesson
pro_course_detail.description:
In this lesson, we may work on pronunciation through:
~ dialogues (beginner through advanced)
~ working through a comprehensive guide on American English (book can be bought by student if desired)
~ listening to videos (advanced)
~ listening to songs (elementary through advanced)

Students will learn about:
~ American vowels, word stress, rhythm, consonants, intonation
~ pronunciation of phrases in connected speech

I'm a native English speaker and speak Standard American English. There are different varieties of spoken English in the US, and if anything, I may speak a "Western" variety of American English since I have spent most of my life on the West Coast. This means I don't make any difference between "cot" and "caught", for example. I studied Clinical Phonetics in speech language pathology and know IPA (the International Phonetic Alphabet). I also may try to relate American English sounds to those in other languages I have studied (French, Japanese, Italian, Chinese, German). 

Although a one-hour lesson is offered, it's not necessarily recommended to take a one-hour pronunciation lesson as it will be fairly tiring. You're welcome to try 30 minutes and see if this lesson is for you. Audio recordings of lessons may be available for review and study if desired, depending on the platform you choose.

By the way, 1 hour lessons can be on italki classroom or Skype. Lessons on Zoom cannot last longer than 40 min.

pro_course_detail.title: American Accent Mastery — Near native speaking and LISTENING skills — see description!
pro_course_detail.description:
Do you want to sound better, and also improve your LISTENING comprehension dramatically? Well, the way you speak is the way you expect to hear. Better listening comprehension means you can enjoy learning using radio, TV and movies — enjoying all the benefits of authentic native-speaker material.

This course can be taken at any time, but it is most advantageous to do so before memorizing thousands of words with inaccurate pronunciation, and before spending countless hours practicing bad prosody in conversations.

No, you will not be able to pass for a native speaker after just one session :) The goal of this course will be to aim for near-native pronunciation while we make steady progress each lesson. Language coaching is provided so you can maximize your self-study outside of our sessions.

My philosophy: You do not need “accent reduction” — you do not need to reduce anything. Your native accent is perfect — for your native language. What you need is accent acquisition — to acquire a subconscious mastery of the characteristic phonology of your target language that will allow you to speak “naturally” and LISTEN as easily as a native.

Depending on your personal goals and what we uncover during our first conversation, we may perfect your consonants, vowels, stress, intonation, rhythm, etc. We can improve all of these at either a basic or advanced level, as needed.

Video or just audio — it’s your decision, as I can tell exactly how you’re using your lips, tongue, etc., just by listening.

The price of this course is a little bit higher than the standard “Conversational English with Integrated Grammar” because 99.9% of English teachers don’t have the skills to teach it. You will experience noticeable improvement after every session — guaranteed. Write me for additional information.
